# The Great Chorus of the Deep

## Scripture
"The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands. Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge. There is no speech or language where their voice is not heard." — Psalm 19:1–3

## Reflection
On a moonless autumn night, far from city lights, you can trace the Milky Way—a luminous river of countless suns. But what our eyes cannot see is the sound: astronomers tell us that across the cosmos, ancient stars and vast clouds of gas sing. They vibrate with frequencies far below human hearing, a deep, ceaseless hum echoing through creation.

In these crisp September evenings, when the Milky Way arches overhead, remember: you are gazing at a choir. Every star, every galaxy, every unseen particle joins in a song of praise that began before time and will never end. And here is the wonder—your voice is part of it too.

Psalm 19 tells us creation's testimony reaches every language and people, no translation needed. Yet God has also given *you* a voice: in your gratitude, your kindness, your quiet faithfulness. When you feel small beneath the stars, remember that the One who set them singing also tuned your heart to praise Him.

## Prayer
Lord of the cosmos, when I stand beneath the Milky Way, I feel both small and deeply loved. Thank You for inviting me into creation's endless song. Teach me to add my voice today—through words and deeds—to the chorus declaring Your glory. Amen.
